examples.knowledge_point: Solving for a Vector in a Linear Combination
examples.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate $\mathbf{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a+2x & =b \\ 2x & =b-a \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}(b-a) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}([\begin{aligned}24 \\ -9 \\ 13\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -11 \\ -5\end{aligned}]) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 2 \\ 18\end{aligned}] \\ x & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 1 \\ 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $m$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}7{a}_{1}+m{a}_{2} & =b \\ 7[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+m[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\ m[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -12\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ m[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From the final equation above, we can tell that $m=-5.$
